advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm retrying the catch-all 'store-read-failure' reason is intended for genuinely-persistent tracker faults (missing .git, dirty tracked worktree, subprocess failure), not only the transient staged-index race the comment describes.
evidence: relation_snapshot.py:146 `if run(*status_args): raise _store_error(...)` — any dirty tracked worktree collapses to store-read-failure
relation_snapshot.py:118-122 missing/invalid tracker dir also raises store-read-failure
relation_snapshot.py:155-156 `except Exception: raise _store_error(...)` — git subprocess timeout/IO failures all collapse to store-read-failure
The comment (generation.py:290-298) scopes the retry to the transient staged-index race, but the reason it keys on is not that narrow
advisory.finding: 'store-read-failure' is a catch-all collapse reason in tracker_head_sha (dirty tracked worktree, unmerged index, missing/invalid tracker dir, malformed HEAD, git subprocess timeout/IO error all map to it). Retrying it reclassifies genuinely persistent, non-transient failures from a terminal PlanReviewGenerationError (unsigned + actionable) into a retryable-after-3 PlanReviewGenerationRetryable, masking real broken-tracker conditions as transient races.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider whether the store-read-failure retry needs a small backoff/jitter between attempts to actually outlast a peer's in-flight git add->commit window.
evidence: search for 'sleep' in generation.py returned (no matches)
advisory.finding: The store-read-failure retry loop performs three retries with no backoff/sleep between attempts, so all three pre-lock reads can sample the same in-flight staged-index window within microseconds and fail identically, making the retry ineffective against the very concurrent race it targets.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that a PlanRelationSnapshotError with a deterministic reason (e.g. 'malformed-reference') raised from the pre-lock reads raises PlanReviewGenerationError terminally on attempt 1 (no retry).
evidence: generation.py:299-308 adds `if exc.reason == "store-read-failure": ... continue` else `raise PlanReviewGenerationError(exc.reason)`, so the retry/terminal split is the new behavior.
The diff's own contract comment states 'Deterministic reasons (missing/ambiguous/malformed/reducer/id-mismatch) stay terminal — retrying cannot fix a genuinely broken reference.'

Named violating input: `PlanRelationSnapshotError("malformed-reference")` raised from the pre-lock `tracker_head_sha`/`collect` reads must produce PlanReviewGenerationError on the first attempt with no retry.

The pre-existing test_terminal_sign_failure_is_structured_and_unsigned (lines 107-117) injects a signer RuntimeError caught by the separate except clause at generation.py:377, not the PlanRelationSnapshotError branch, so it does not cover this path.
Both new tests use only reason='store-read-failure'; no test exercises the else branch at generation.py:307-308.
advisory.finding: No test asserts the terminal (non-retried) side of the newly added PlanRelationSnapshotError discriminator: a deterministic reason (e.g. 'malformed-reference') must still raise PlanReviewGenerationError terminally, not be retried. A regression that broadened the retry guard to all reasons would pass every existing test.
scenarios: A future refactor drops or inverts the `if exc.reason == "store-read-failure"` guard, causing deterministic broken references (missing/malformed target) to be silently retried and surfaced as retryable instead of terminal.
A deterministic error is misclassified and retried MAX_GENERATION_ATTEMPTS times, delaying a clear terminal failure.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test mirroring test_persistent_store_read_failure_is_retryable_not_terminal but with reason='malformed-reference', asserting pytest.raises(generation.PlanReviewGenerationError) and that the 'plan_review_sign_aborted' log record is emitted with attempt==1 (proving no retry occurred).
